info.name: ClinicalHarmony · Phase 5b slice 4 — SMART on FHIR (Keycloak)
info.description: SMART on FHIR backend services: Keycloak client_credentials tokens (0b stores a full-scope token; 40 stores a narrow system/Coverage.rs token in narrow_token), the public SMART discovery document, and the 401/403 rules — OperationOutcomes on /fhir/**, plain JSON elsewhere, insufficient_scope naming the missing scope. Make sure `docker-compose up -d` is running. Run '0b. Auth' first: it does a client_credentials grant against Keycloak (realm clinicalharmony, {{keycloak_url}}) and stores the token in the collection variable access_token, which every request inherits via the collection's Bearer auth (public endpoints ignore it). Tokens live 5 minutes — re-run 0b when you get 401s.

request.description: Expect: 200 OK, body `{"status":"UP"}`. If this fails, the container isn't running — check `docker ps` for clinicalharmony-fhir-compliance-service.

SMART Backend Services-style client_credentials grant (client secret via HTTP Basic). Requests every SMART read scope plus the clinicalharmony/pipeline.write operational scope; the test script stores the token in {{access_token}}, which the collection's Bearer auth sends on every request. Expect: 200 with access_token, token_type Bearer, expires_in 300, and scope echoing what was granted.

Public, no token. Expect: 200 JSON pointing at the Keycloak realm — issuer, token_endpoint, jwks_uri; grant_types_supported [client_credentials]; capabilities incl. client-confidential-symmetric + permission-v2; scopes_supported lists system/<Type>.rs for the 5 CMS-0057 types, system/*.rs and clinicalharmony/pipeline.write.

item.name: 37. SMART — discovery at the FHIR base (spec location)

request.description: Same document at [FHIR base]/.well-known/smart-configuration, where the SMART spec says clients look. Public.
Expect: 401, application/fhir+json OperationOutcome with issue code 'login', a WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="clinicalharmony" header, and the X-Correlation-Id you sent echoed back.
Expect: 401 OperationOutcome; WWW-Authenticate carries error="invalid_token" and the reason in error_description.

item.name: 40. Auth — get a NARROW token (system/Coverage.rs only)

request.description: Stores a token that can only read/search Coverage in {{narrow_token}}, used by requests 41-43.
system/Coverage.rs grants both read (r) and search (s) on Coverage. Expect: 200.

Expect: 403 OperationOutcome with issue code 'forbidden' naming the missing scope (system/MeasureReport.s), and WWW-Authenticate: Bearer ... error="insufficient_scope", scope="system/MeasureReport.s".

item.name: 43. Auth — narrow token on gold/revalidate → 403 (needs pipeline.write)

request.description: Gold writers need clinicalharmony/pipeline.write. Off /fhir the error keeps this service's usual shape: {"error":"Forbidden","message":"...clinicalharmony/pipeline.write"}.

item.name: 44. Auth — no token on build → 401 (plain JSON)

request.description: Expect: 401 {"error":"Unauthorized",...} — not an OperationOutcome, since this isn't a FHIR endpoint.
